findings.issue_text: P2: Authorization logic inverted in addGuests.handler.ts:46-48 — isTeamAdminOrOwner uses && instead of ||, collapsing the check to owner-only so team admins who should be able to add guests to team bookings get FORBIDDEN

P2: Blacklist bypass via case variation in addGuests.handler.ts:71-79 — blacklist entries are lowercased but guest emails are tested raw, so submitting e.g. Spam@Example.com completely defeats the BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS abuse-control mechanism

P2: No server-side dedupe of guests — addGuests.schema.ts only validates z.array(z.string().email()) without the uniqueness refine (which exists only in the client), and the handler never dedupes within the guests array itself, so an API caller can send duplicate emails and create duplicate attendee rows and duplicated ics attendees
P2: Case-sensitive dedupe against existing attendees (guest === attendee.email) means User@X.com vs stored user@x.com creates a duplicate row for the same mailbox
P2: When all submitted guests are filtered out because they already exist as attendees, the handler throws emails_must_be_unique_valid, which misdescribes the actual problem (already an attendee)

P2: Calendar update runs with the acting user's credentials instead of the organizer's — getUsersCredentials(ctx.user) builds the EventManager from the caller while booking.user is fetched with credentials: true but never used, so for non-organizer authorized paths updateCalendarAttendees targets calendars it cannot access and attendee updates fail or silently no-op

P2: DB write not compensated on later failure — attendees are persisted before updateCalendarAttendees, which is not wrapped in try/catch; if the calendar call throws, the mutation errors while guests were saved, and a retry then hits uniqueGuests.length === 0 and returns the misleading BAD_REQUEST emails_must_be_unique_valid with calendar and emails never completed

P2: No booking.status check in the handler — guests can be added to cancelled/rejected bookings, sending emails with an ICS attachment using method: REQUEST / status: CONFIRMED that resurrects the cancelled event in attendees' calendar clients

P2: Seated event types have no capacity check and no seat records — seatsPerTimeSlot is copied onto evt but never enforced, so guests beyond seat capacity are inserted as plain attendees without BookingSeat records, breaking seat-based invariants (capacity limits, seat management, seatsShowAttendees behavior)

P3: Validation error state never reset on success in AddGuestsDialog.tsx:36-41 — onSuccess resets multiEmailValue and closes the dialog but does not call setIsInvalidEmail(false), so after a failed attempt followed by a successful add, reopening the dialog shows the stale 'Emails must be unique and valid' error against a blank form

P3: Dead fallback in error toast in AddGuestsDialog.tsx:42-45 — the template literal is always truthy so the unable_to_add_guests fallback is unreachable; when err.data?.code is absent the user sees 'undefined: …', and t(err.message) on non-i18n messages renders raw internals

P3: Email failures swallowed without the error in addGuests.handler.ts:168-172 — the catch block only console.logs a static message, discarding err entirely (no message, no stack), while the caller receives a success toast, making any email outage undiagnosable and invisible to the user

P3: booking.userId || 0 turns a null organizer into an unhandled 500 in addGuests.handler.ts:58-61 — for bookings with null userId, the id: 0 query matches nothing and findFirstOrThrow throws a raw Prisma P2025 that surfaces as an opaque 500 instead of a handled NOT_FOUND/BAD_REQUEST

Team admin authorization logic inverted: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` uses `&&` instead of `||`, requiring both admin AND owner status; since isTeamOwner is a strict subset of isTeamAdmin, this resolves to owner-only, causing team admins who aren't owners to get a 403 on a feature they should be able to use (addGuests.handler.ts:45-47)
Redundant double DB calls: the `&&` condition evaluates both isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner when a single check would suffice (addGuests.handler.ts:45-47)

No cap on guest count: `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` has no `.max()` and the handler applies no limit, allowing one authenticated request to inject thousands of attendees and trigger unbounded email fan-out via sendAddGuestsEmails (mail-bombing / resource-exhaustion vector) (addGuests.schema.ts:5, addGuests.handler.ts:72-76)

BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS blocklist bypass via case mismatch: blocklist entries are lowercased but the incoming guest email is compared as-is, so `EVIL@x.com` bypasses a blacklist entry of `evil@x.com` (addGuests.handler.ts:68-76)

Case-sensitive existing-attendee dedupe: `guest === attendee.email` comparison doesn't lowercase the guest email, allowing case-variant duplicates of already-registered attendees (addGuests.handler.ts:68-76)

Any booking attendee can add guests to a booking they don't own: the permission check grants full add-guests rights to isAttendee, letting a non-owner trigger organizer-identity emails (with meeting details, video-call link, and replyTo set to the organizer's address) and ics REQUEST invites to arbitrary addresses with no organizer confirmation step (addGuests.handler.ts:49-55)

No booking status check: the handler never validates booking.status, so guests can be added to cancelled/rejected/pending bookings, and the email templates hardcode status CONFIRMED with method REQUEST, pushing a CONFIRMED invite that re-adds a cancelled meeting to attendees' calendars (addGuests.handler.ts:25-43, attendee-add-guests-email.ts:12-19, organizer-add-guests-email.ts:13-20)

Guest uniqueness enforced only client-side: the server schema doesn't dedupe guests and the handler filter only removes emails matching existing attendees, not duplicates within the request array, so a direct API call with duplicate emails creates duplicate attendee rows or a Prisma P2002 → 500 (addGuests.schema.ts:5, addGuests.handler.ts:72-76)

Case-sensitive email comparisons cause false denials and misclassified emails: `attendee.email === user.email` (addGuests.handler.ts:51) and `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` (email-manager.ts:~543) compare emails without case normalization

Unbounded `guests` input array in addGuests.schema.ts has no .max() cap, allowing any authenticated user to trigger unbounded DB inserts (createMany), a concurrent email fan-out via Promise.all, and an O(N×A) dedup scan — a spam/deliverability and cost vector with memory/latency spikes

Email fan-out in email-manager.ts re-notifies organizer, team members, and ALL attendees (existing and new) on every add-guests call, with each email embedding a full-ICS render making aggregate cost ~O(A²) in attendee count; for seated events the attendee list accumulates indefinitely so each subsequent call gets more expensive
Organizer email's Reply-To header contains every attendee address (organizer-add-guests-email.ts), which approaches SMTP header limits at scale

Unused `credentials` include in addGuests.handler.ts over-fetches all credential rows for the booking owner (including encrypted key material) on every call, causing wasted I/O and unnecessary in-memory exposure of credential payloads

Heavy multi-include fetch (attendees, references, eventType, owner + credentials) in addGuests.handler.ts executes before the authorization check for any bookingId from any authenticated user, enabling cheap-for-attacker full-materialization probing; NOT_FOUND throws before FORBIDDEN so booking existence is also enumerable

AddGuestsDialog.tsx calls utils.viewer.bookings.invalidate() at router level, refetching every active viewer.bookings.* query (including the heavy bookings list with per-row attendees/payment/eventType includes) when only the query showing this booking needs refreshing

getTranslation is awaited per attendee in addGuests.handler.ts (including pre-existing attendees) instead of deduped per distinct locale, repeating i18n instantiation N times when the result depends only on locale
The isTeamAdmin && isTeamOwner check in addGuests.handler.ts requires BOTH roles while the variable name says AdminOrOwner — either non-owner admins are wrongly denied or the team path is unreachable
The evt built in the handler never sets team, so the calendarEvent.team?.members branch in sendAddGuestsEmails (email-manager.ts:529) is unreachable and team members likely never notified

P2 — Team admin/owner check uses `&&` instead of `||` in `isTeamAdminOrOwner`, collapsing the permission to owner-only and denying team admins (who aren't owners) the ability to add guests to their team's bookings

P2 — Server schema is weaker than the client contract: `guests` array has no uniqueness validation or case normalization, so duplicate or case-variant emails produce duplicate attendee rows, duplicate emails, and duplicated ICS attendees

P2 — `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS` check is bypassable via letter case: blacklist entries are lowercased but the incoming guest email is compared raw, so case-variant blacklisted emails pass the filter and still receive emails

P2 — Unbounded `guests` array (no `.max()` on the zod schema) creates an email-amplification/resource-abuse vector: any attendee can submit thousands of guests or repeatedly re-trigger emails to all participants

P2 — Calendar attendee update runs with the caller's credentials instead of the organizer's, so `updateCalendarAttendees` silently fails (or errors after persistence) for non-organizer callers, leaving calendar out of sync; credentials should come from `booking.user`

P2 — No seats-capacity handling for seated event types: `seatsPerTimeSlot` is never enforced and no `BookingSeat` records are created, allowing overbooking beyond capacity and attendees in an inconsistent state
P3 — `findFirstOrThrow` with `booking.userId || 0` yields an unhandled Prisma error surfacing as a generic 500 instead of a clean `TRPCError` when `booking.userId` is null

addGuests.handler.ts:165 — updateCalendarAttendees runs unguarded after the DB commit with no try/catch, creating an unrecoverable partial-failure state where DB, calendar, and emails become inconsistent and retries are permanently blocked by the uniqueness filter

addGuests.handler.ts:158-163 — EventManager is built with the actor's credentials instead of the booking owner's, so when an attendee or team admin adds guests to someone else's booking the calendar event's attendee list is silently never updated
addGuests.handler.ts:46-48 — authorization uses isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...) instead of ||, so team admins get FORBIDDEN even though the UI exposes the Add guests action on team bookings

addGuests.handler.ts:70-78 + addGuests.schema.ts:5 — no server-side dedupe or case normalization: duplicate emails in one batch create duplicate attendee rows, and case variants bypass both the existing-attendee check and the BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS blacklist

addGuests.schema.ts:5 — the guests array has no .max() cap and the handler imposes no limit, allowing a single request to create thousands of attendee rows and trigger unbounded synchronous email fan-out (resource exhaustion and mail-spam vector)

addGuests.handler.ts:26-56 — no booking.status validation, so guests can be added to cancelled/rejected/pending bookings and new guests receive a CONFIRMED ICS REQUEST that resurrects a cancelled meeting in their calendars

addGuests.handler.ts:92-106 — seated bookings bypass seat accounting: attendees are created via plain createMany with no BookingSeat records and no capacity check, allowing seated events to be overbooked
addGuests.handler.ts:167-171 — email failures are swallowed with console.log, with no detailed logging, error tracking, or retry, causing silent partial failure while the mutation returns success

addGuests.handler.ts:58-68 — findFirstOrThrow on booking.userId || 0 throws a raw Prisma P2025 error instead of a TRPCError when booking.userId is null, giving the client an opaque 500 instead of a meaningful handled error
AddGuestsDialog.tsx:33,56 — isInvalidEmail is never reset on success or non-cancel close (ESC/overlay), so reopening the dialog shows a stale error banner over a fresh form

AddGuestsDialog.tsx:48-57 — leftover empty rows fail the whole batch: the client zod schema validates every entry including empty strings with no filtering of blanks, so a user leaving one empty row cannot submit at all

Authorization conjunction bug in addGuests.handler.ts:46-48: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` uses `&&` instead of `||`, requiring both admin AND owner; since isTeamAdmin already returns true for owners, this is logically equivalent to isTeamOwner alone, making the isTeamAdmin call dead weight and incorrectly denying team admins (non-owners) with FORBIDDEN, plus wasting a DB roundtrip per request

Calendar update in addGuests.handler.ts:150-155 uses the acting user's credentials (getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)) instead of the booking organizer's credentials; for attendee/admin flows, updateCalendarAttendees either no-ops or updates the organizer's external event with the wrong user's client, even though booking.user.credentials is queried but never used

Case-sensitive email dedupe and blacklist check in addGuests.handler.ts:74-78: exact-match comparisons against a lowercased blacklist allow adding User@X.com when user@x.com already attends, causing duplicate attendee rows, duplicate invitation emails, duplicated calendar attendees, and trivial blacklist bypass via casing

Duplicated validation between AddGuestsDialog.tsx:26-29 and addGuests.schema.ts:3-6 has diverged: the client redefines the Zod schema inside the component (recreated every render) with a uniqueness refine the server schema lacks; the server never dedupes within the input, so duplicate guests like ["a@b.com", "a@b.com"] pass validation and createMany inserts two identical attendee rows

No gating on booking status or time in addGuests.handler.ts:44-56: guests can be added to cancelled, rejected, pending, or past bookings, and the hardcoded ICS method: "REQUEST" with status: "CONFIRMED" in the new email templates can resurrect a cancelled event on attendees' calendars

Partial-failure state with no recovery path in addGuests.handler.ts:92-102 vs :157: attendees are persisted before updateCalendarAttendees runs unguarded; if it throws, guests are in the DB but the mutation errors, and retry dead-ends because the dedupe filter matches all guests and throws BAD_REQUEST, with no way to remove attendees
Error swallowed and unloggable in addGuests.handler.ts:161-163: catch block discards err entirely and logs a static string, making email failures undebuggable in production

Raw input passed instead of filtered list in addGuests.handler.ts:160: sendAddGuestsEmails receives raw guests instead of uniqueGuests, so an existing attendee re-entered in the form receives a full AttendeeScheduledEmail invitation instead of the 'guests added' notice

Misleading reused error key in addGuests.handler.ts:80-81: when all provided guests are duplicates/already attending, the handler throws emails_must_be_unique_valid ('Emails must be unique and valid'), which doesn't describe the actual problem and is surfaced verbatim to the user

Stale validation state never cleared in AddGuestsDialog.tsx:33,36-45: isInvalidEmail is only reset by the Cancel button (not on input change, success, or reopen), so the error banner persists while fixing emails and reappears on next open; email state also survives ESC/overlay close

Dead fallback and i18n-key abuse in AddGuestsDialog.tsx:43-44: message || t("unable_to_add_guests") is unreachable because message is a template literal and always truthy, and t(err.message) treats arbitrary error text as a translation key, surfacing raw keys/messages to users

Hardcoded English in shared UI package at packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx:47: <Tooltip content="Remove email"> is a literal string in a reusable, otherwise-t()-translated component exported from @calcom/ui, making it untranslatable for all consumers

Full payload duplication in attendee-add-guests-email.ts and organizer-add-guests-email.ts: both classes copy the entire getNodeMailerPayload from their base classes to change only title/subject, so future changes to base payload logic must be manually mirrored in both copies

Seats-enabled bookings unguarded in addGuests.handler.ts: no check on booking.eventType.seatsPerTimeSlot, so plain attendees are created without seat references and all attendees are pushed to the calendar event, bypassing seat-capacity accounting and the seats flow's attendee handling

booking.userId || 0 into findFirstOrThrow in addGuests.handler.ts:58-60: booking.userId is nullable; a null value becomes id: 0 and surfaces as an unhandled Prisma P2025 (500) rather than a proper TRPCError

No booking-status validation in addGuests.handler.ts — guests can be added to cancelled/pending/rejected bookings, triggering 'confirmed' ICS REQUEST attachments and 'your event is scheduled' emails for dead meetings (correctness bug and mild phishing/spam vector)
isTeamAdminOrOwner uses && instead of || in addGuests.handler.ts:46-48 — requires user to be both admin and owner, collapsing to owner-only so team admins get FORBIDDEN and can never use the feature

EventManager built from the acting user's credentials instead of the organizer's in addGuests.handler.ts:149-154 — fetched booking.user.credentials are never used; for non-organizer actors, updateCalendarAttendees runs against the wrong calendar account so the organizer's calendar event never gets the new attendees

Non-atomic partial failure: DB write commits before calendar/email steps in addGuests.handler.ts — if updateCalendarAttendees throws, the mutation 500s after attendees are already in the DB, and retries are rejected by the dedup filter with misleading emails_must_be_unique_valid error

Email failures swallowed in addGuests.handler.ts:158-162 — catch block only console.logs and success is returned unconditionally, so the client shows 'Guests added' success toast even if every email send failed; also uses console.log instead of structured logging

Email normalization missing in addGuests.handler.ts:66-74 — blacklist entries are lowercased but guest emails are not, so 'Spam@x.com' bypasses blacklist entry 'spam@x.com'; same case-sensitivity in the attendee-dedup check creates duplicate attendee rows

evt.team is never populated in addGuests.handler.ts:112-140 — calendarEvent.team?.members gate in email-manager.ts never runs, so for team bookings only the booking owner gets the organizer email and other booked hosts are never notified about added guests

Unbounded guests array (no max() on z.array in addGuests.schema.ts) with no rate limiting, combined with attendee authorization path — any authenticated attendee on any booking can create thousands of attendee rows and trigger thousands of invite emails in a single API call (email-bombing vector)

No server-side uniqueness within a request — uniqueness refine exists only in the client dialog; direct API calls with duplicate emails pass the schema and createMany inserts duplicate attendee rows, with no unique constraint to prevent concurrent request races

findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } }) in addGuests.handler.ts:58-59 — Booking.userId is nullable; when null this queries id 0 and throws an unhandled Prisma error resulting in a raw 500 instead of a meaningful TRPC error

isInvalidEmail never reset on success in AddGuestsDialog.tsx:33-38 — onSuccess resets emails and closes the dialog but not isInvalidEmail, so reopening shows the stale 'Emails must be unique and valid' banner before any input

additional_guests locale key not added in this diff — BookingListItem.tsx and AddGuestsDialog.tsx use t('additional_guests') but the locale diff only adds other keys; if the key doesn't already exist, the action label and dialog title render the raw key

If all submitted guests are already attendees, `uniqueGuests.length === 0` and it throws `TRPCError({ code: "BAD_REQUEST", message: "emails_must_be_unique_valid" })`, which is misleading because the emails may be valid/unique but simply already added. adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the calendar update is executed via `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` where `eventManager` is constructed from the acting user (`...user` from `ctx.user`) and `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`. The booking’s organizer user is fetched with `include: { credentials: true }` under `booking.user`, but those credentials are never used. For authorized non-organizer paths (e.g., an attendee adding guests, which is explicitly allowed by `isAttendee`), the caller typically won’t have access to the organizer’s connected calendar, so `updateCalendarAttendees` may fail or no-op, meaning guests aren’t actually added to the external calendar even though the DB update succeeds.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: DB write not compensated on later failure — attendees are persisted before updateCalendarAttendees, which is not wrapped in try/catch; if the calendar call throws, the mutation errors while guests were saved, and a retry then hits uniqueGuests.length === 0 and returns the misleading BAD_REQUEST emails_must_be_unique_valid with calendar and emails never completed

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the mutation persists new attendees via `prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)` before calling `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);`. That calendar update is not wrapped in `try/catch` or a DB transaction, so if it throws, the TRPC mutation errors while the DB write has already succeeded. On a subsequent retry, `uniqueGuests` is computed by filtering out emails already present in `booking.attendees`, so it can become empty and the handler throws `BAD_REQUEST` with `emails_must_be_unique_valid`, which is misleading and also means the calendar update + email sending may never complete for those already-persisted guests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: No booking.status check in the handler — guests can be added to cancelled/rejected bookings, sending emails with an ICS attachment using method: REQUEST / status: CONFIRMED that resurrects the cancelled event in attendees' calendar clients

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuestsHandler` (new file `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts`), the booking is fetched and then attendees are appended and calendar/email updates are sent, but there is no check of any booking lifecycle/status (e.g., cancelled/rejected) before proceeding. The email templates generated in `packages/emails/templates/*-add-guests-email.ts` attach an ICS with `method: "REQUEST"` and `status: "CONFIRMED"`, which would be inappropriate for a cancelled/rejected booking and could cause calendar clients to (re-)add/confirm the event. This is directly grounded in the diff: the handler never guards on status, and the ICS payload is always CONFIRMED.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Seated event types have no capacity check and no seat records — seatsPerTimeSlot is copied onto evt but never enforced, so guests beyond seat capacity are inserted as plain attendees without BookingSeat records, breaking seat-based invariants (capacity limits, seat management, seatsShowAttendees behavior)

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, new guests are persisted via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` with no check against `booking.eventType?.seatsPerTimeSlot` (seated capacity) and no creation of any seat-specific records—guests are added as plain `attendees`. Yet the generated `CalendarEvent` includes `seatsPerTimeSlot`/`seatsShowAttendees` and is passed to `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`, implying seat-aware behavior elsewhere. This means seated event bookings can be overfilled and/or have seat-based invariants broken by this new endpoint.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: Validation error state never reset on success in AddGuestsDialog.tsx:36-41 — onSuccess resets multiEmailValue and closes the dialog but does not call setIsInvalidEmail(false), so after a failed attempt followed by a successful add, reopening the dialog shows the stale 'Emails must be unique and valid' error against a blank form

adjudication.rationale: In AddGuestsDialog, `isInvalidEmail` is set to `true` on validation failure (`setIsInvalidEmail(true)` in `handleAdd`), but the mutation `onSuccess` handler only calls `setIsOpenDialog(false)` and `setMultiEmailValue([""])` and never resets `isInvalidEmail` to `false`. Since the dialog component stays mounted (it’s always rendered in `BookingListItem` and controlled via `open`), reopening it after a successful add can still show the stale error banner even with a reset/blank email input.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: Dead fallback in error toast in AddGuestsDialog.tsx:42-45 — the template literal is always truthy so the unable_to_add_guests fallback is unreachable; when err.data?.code is absent the user sees 'undefined: …', and t(err.message) on non-i18n messages renders raw internals

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog.tsx` the `onError` handler builds `const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`;` and then calls `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), "error")`. A template literal always produces a (truthy) string, so the `unable_to_add_guests` fallback is effectively unreachable. When `err.data?.code` is missing, the toast will display `undefined: ...`, matching the finding. The diff clearly introduces this behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: Email failures swallowed without the error in addGuests.handler.ts:168-172 — the catch block only console.logs a static message, discarding err entirely (no message, no stack), while the caller receives a success toast, making any email outage undiagnosable and invisible to the user

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the `sendAddGuestsEmails` call is wrapped in `try/catch`, and the catch block only does `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")` without logging/propagating `err` (no message/stack). The handler then still returns success (`return { message: "Guests added" }`) and the UI shows a success toast on mutation success, so email delivery failures are effectively silent and hard to diagnose. This is a concrete, diff-grounded observability/UX issue, but not necessarily a functional defect since guests are still added and calendar attendees are updated before the email attempt.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: booking.userId || 0 turns a null organizer into an unhandled 500 in addGuests.handler.ts:58-61 — for bookings with null userId, the id: 0 query matches nothing and findFirstOrThrow throws a raw Prisma P2025 that surfaces as an opaque 500 instead of a handled NOT_FOUND/BAD_REQUEST

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the organizer is loaded via `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } })`. If `booking.userId` is `null`/`undefined` (which the `|| 0` suggests is possible), this will query `id: 0` and `findFirstOrThrow` will throw an unhandled Prisma error rather than a controlled `TRPCError` like `NOT_FOUND`/`BAD_REQUEST`. The handler does not catch this exception, so it would surface as a 500.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Team admin authorization logic inverted: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` uses `&&` instead of `||`, requiring both admin AND owner status; since isTeamOwner is a strict subset of isTeamAdmin, this resolves to owner-only, causing team admins who aren't owners to get a 403 on a feature they should be able to use (addGuests.handler.ts:45-47)

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`, which requires the user to be both a team admin and a team owner to pass the authorization check. The variable name and typical permission intent imply admin OR owner should be sufficient; as written, a non-owner admin would fail `isTeamAdminOrOwner` and (if not organizer/attendee) hit the `FORBIDDEN` branch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Redundant double DB calls: the `&&` condition evaluates both isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner when a single check would suffice (addGuests.handler.ts:45-47)

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed via two separate awaited calls: `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`. This can result in two sequential DB-backed permission checks when the first returns true, which is a concrete performance/efficiency concern introduced by the diff. However, the finding’s claim that `&&` “evaluates both” unconditionally is imprecise because `&&` short-circuits (the second call won’t run if `isTeamAdmin` is false), and whether a single check truly suffices isn’t provable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No cap on guest count: `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` has no `.max()` and the handler applies no limit, allowing one authenticated request to inject thousands of attendees and trigger unbounded email fan-out via sendAddGuestsEmails (mail-bombing / resource-exhaustion vector) (addGuests.schema.ts:5, addGuests.handler.ts:72-76)

adjudication.rationale: Verified: the new TRPC input schema allows an unbounded array (`guests: z.array(z.string().email())` in `addGuests.schema.ts`) with no `.max()`, and the handler enforces no upper limit—only filters out existing/blacklisted emails (`uniqueGuests = guests.filter(...)`). It then persists all remaining guests via `createMany` and triggers email sending over the full attendee list (`sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` after `booking.update(...)`), which can scale linearly with the injected guest count (and also increases calendar update work via `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees`). This enables a single authenticated call to create a very large number of attendees and cause large outbound email fan-out/resource exhaustion.

adjudication_records.issue_text: BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS blocklist bypass via case mismatch: blocklist entries are lowercased but the incoming guest email is compared as-is, so `EVIL@x.com` bypasses a blacklist entry of `evil@x.com` (addGuests.handler.ts:68-76)

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS` entries are normalized to lowercase (`.map((email) => email.toLowerCase())`), but the filter checks `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` without lowercasing `guest`. This makes the blacklist case-sensitive on input, so an input like `EVIL@x.com` would not match a blacklist entry `evil@x.com` and would be allowed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Case-sensitive existing-attendee dedupe: `guest === attendee.email` comparison doesn't lowercase the guest email, allowing case-variant duplicates of already-registered attendees (addGuests.handler.ts:68-76)

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `uniqueGuests` is computed with a case-sensitive comparison against existing attendees: `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)`. Since the input schema only validates format (`z.string().email()`) and does not normalize casing, a guest like `Test@ex.com` can bypass the dedupe when an existing attendee email is `test@ex.com`, resulting in duplicate attendees being created via `createMany` and potentially duplicate notifications/calendar updates.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Any booking attendee can add guests to a booking they don't own: the permission check grants full add-guests rights to isAttendee, letting a non-owner trigger organizer-identity emails (with meeting details, video-call link, and replyTo set to the organizer's address) and ics REQUEST invites to arbitrary addresses with no organizer confirmation step (addGuests.handler.ts:49-55)

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the permission gate explicitly allows any existing attendee to add guests: `const isAttendee = !!booking.attendees.find((attendee) => attendee.email === user.email);` and the request is permitted if `!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee` is false (i.e., `isAttendee` true) (around the shown block). Once permitted, the handler updates the booking attendees and then calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` and `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`, which sends organizer/attendee emails (with ICS REQUESTs in the email templates) without any organizer confirmation. This matches the finding that a non-owner attendee can trigger invites/emails to arbitrary addresses by adding guests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No booking status check: the handler never validates booking.status, so guests can be added to cancelled/rejected/pending bookings, and the email templates hardcode status CONFIRMED with method REQUEST, pushing a CONFIRMED invite that re-adds a cancelled meeting to attendees' calendars (addGuests.handler.ts:25-43, attendee-add-guests-email.ts:12-19, organizer-add-guests-email.ts:13-20)

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuestsHandler` updates the booking attendees and calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` without any guard on `booking.status` (it fetches `prisma.booking.findFirst({ where: { id: bookingId }, ... })` and never checks status before updating). Separately, the new email templates always generate an ICS payload with `status: "CONFIRMED"` and `method: "REQUEST"` (see `packages/emails/templates/attendee-add-guests-email.ts` and `packages/emails/templates/organizer-add-guests-email.ts`). If a booking is cancelled/rejected/etc., this combination can send a confirmed calendar request/update and potentially re-add/confirm an event for attendees, which is incorrect behavior for non-confirmed bookings.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Guest uniqueness enforced only client-side: the server schema doesn't dedupe guests and the handler filter only removes emails matching existing attendees, not duplicates within the request array, so a direct API call with duplicate emails creates duplicate attendee rows or a Prisma P2002 → 500 (addGuests.schema.ts:5, addGuests.handler.ts:72-76)

adjudication.rationale: The server-side input schema `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts) only validates `guests` as `z.array(z.string().email())` with no uniqueness constraint. In the handler, `uniqueGuests` is computed via `guests.filter(...)` (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts) but the predicate only excludes emails already in `booking.attendees` and blacklisted emails; it does not remove duplicates within the incoming `guests` array. Those duplicates are then passed to `attendees.createMany` (same handler), which can create duplicate attendee rows or trigger a Prisma unique constraint error if such a constraint exists—either way, it's incorrect behavior compared to the client-side uniqueness refine.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Case-sensitive email comparisons cause false denials and misclassified emails: `attendee.email === user.email` (addGuests.handler.ts:51) and `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` (email-manager.ts:~543) compare emails without case normalization

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces case-sensitive email equality checks that can lead to incorrect behavior. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, attendee permission is determined via `booking.attendees.find((attendee) => attendee.email === user.email)`, which will fail if the same email differs only by case, potentially causing a false FORBIDDEN. In `sendAddGuestsEmails` (`email-manager.ts`), `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` is also case-sensitive; since `newGuests` comes from raw input (`guests`) and `attendee.email` comes from stored/normalized values, casing mismatches can misclassify an attendee as “new” vs “existing”, resulting in the wrong email template being sent.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unbounded `guests` input array in addGuests.schema.ts has no .max() cap, allowing any authenticated user to trigger unbounded DB inserts (createMany), a concurrent email fan-out via Promise.all, and an O(N×A) dedup scan — a spam/deliverability and cost vector with memory/latency spikes

adjudication.rationale: Diff adds `addGuests` mutation with input schema `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` in `addGuests.schema.ts` with no `.max(...)` or other server-side bound. Handler `addGuests.handler.ts` then (1) maps `guests` into `uniqueGuests` via `booking.attendees.some(...)` inside a `.filter(...)` (O(N×A) w.r.t. input size × existing attendees), (2) performs `prisma.booking.update(... createMany: { data: guestsFullDetails })` which can insert arbitrarily many rows, and (3) calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` which builds `emailsToSend` and `await Promise.all(emailsToSend)` fanning out emails across attendees. Since this is an authed procedure and client-side checks can be bypassed, an authorized user (organizer/attendee/team admin/owner per diff) could submit a very large `guests` array causing DB, memory, and email-spam/cost amplification. This is a verifiable security/availability defect introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email fan-out in email-manager.ts re-notifies organizer, team members, and ALL attendees (existing and new) on every add-guests call, with each email embedding a full-ICS render making aggregate cost ~O(A²) in attendee count; for seated events the attendee list accumulates indefinitely so each subsequent call gets more expensive

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds sendAddGuestsEmails() in packages/emails/email-manager.ts which (1) always sends an OrganizerAddGuestsEmail to the organizer and each team member (lines adding OrganizerAddGuestsEmail + team.members loop), and (2) iterates over calendarEvent.attendees and sends an email for every attendee on each add-guests call. In addGuests.handler.ts, evt.attendees is built from bookingAttendees.attendees (i.e., the full accumulated attendee list after the update), and the new email templates generate an ICS payload from the full calEvent (see attendee-add-guests-email.ts and organizer-add-guests-email.ts calling generateIcsString({ event: this.calEvent, ... })). That means each call sends O(A) emails each embedding an ICS containing O(A) attendee data, yielding an O(A^2) scaling concern as attendees grow. This is a real, diff-grounded performance/operational cost issue, but not a correctness defect per se.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Organizer email's Reply-To header contains every attendee address (organizer-add-guests-email.ts), which approaches SMTP header limits at scale

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/emails/templates/organizer-add-guests-email.ts`, the nodemailer payload sets `replyTo: [this.calEvent.organizer.email, ...this.calEvent.attendees.map(({ email }) => email)]`, which explicitly includes *all* attendee emails in the Reply-To header. This could become large for bookings with many attendees/guests and may run into practical SMTP/header length limits; it’s a scale/robustness concern grounded in the diff rather than a guaranteed immediate correctness break.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unused `credentials` include in addGuests.handler.ts over-fetches all credential rows for the booking owner (including encrypted key material) on every call, causing wasted I/O and unnecessary in-memory exposure of credential payloads

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the booking query includes `user: { include: { destinationCalendar: true, credentials: true } }`, but `booking.user.credentials` is never referenced afterward. Credentials are instead fetched via `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`. This makes the `credentials: true` include an unnecessary over-fetch of sensitive credential rows into memory and adds avoidable I/O, even if not directly leaked by the code shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Heavy multi-include fetch (attendees, references, eventType, owner + credentials) in addGuests.handler.ts executes before the authorization check for any bookingId from any authenticated user, enabling cheap-for-attacker full-materialization probing; NOT_FOUND throws before FORBIDDEN so booking existence is also enumerable

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the handler does `prisma.booking.findFirst({ where: { id: bookingId }, include: { attendees: true, eventType: true, destinationCalendar: true, references: true, user: { include: { destinationCalendar: true, credentials: true }}}})` before any permission check. It then throws `NOT_FOUND` if no booking, and only afterwards checks access and throws `FORBIDDEN`. This makes booking existence enumerable (different error path) and also forces a relatively heavy multi-include materialization for arbitrary `bookingId` values from any authenticated caller, even when ultimately unauthorized.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AddGuestsDialog.tsx calls utils.viewer.bookings.invalidate() at router level, refetching every active viewer.bookings.* query (including the heavy bookings list with per-row attendees/payment/eventType includes) when only the query showing this booking needs refreshing

adjudication.rationale: In AddGuestsDialog.tsx, the mutation onSuccess calls `utils.viewer.bookings.invalidate();`, which (per tRPC react-query utils semantics) invalidates the whole `viewer.bookings` router scope rather than a specific query key. This can cause refetching of all active `viewer.bookings.*` queries, potentially including the bookings list and other heavier queries, even though only data related to the single updated booking needs refreshing. This is a performance/scope concern grounded in the diff, not a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: getTranslation is awaited per attendee in addGuests.handler.ts (including pre-existing attendees) instead of deduped per distinct locale, repeating i18n instantiation N times when the result depends only on locale

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `attendeesListPromises` maps over `bookingAttendees.attendees` (which includes pre-existing attendees plus newly created ones) and does `translate: await getTranslation(attendee.locale ?? "en", "common")` for each attendee. Since the translation function depends only on `locale`, this repeats i18n loading/instantiation N times for attendees sharing the same locale and could be deduped/cached per distinct locale. This is a performance/efficiency concern, not a correctness defect shown by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The isTeamAdmin && isTeamOwner check in addGuests.handler.ts requires BOTH roles while the variable name says AdminOrOwner — either non-owner admins are wrongly denied or the team path is unreachable

adjudication.rationale:
In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed with `&&`:
```ts
const isTeamAdminOrOwner =
  (await isTeamAdmin(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0)) &&
  (await isTeamOwner(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0));
```
This requires the user to be BOTH a team admin and a team owner, contradicting the `AdminOrOwner` naming and likely intended authorization (“admin OR owner”). As written, a user who is only an admin (or only an owner) would fail this branch and could be incorrectly denied unless they match `isOrganizer`/`isAttendee`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The evt built in the handler never sets team, so the calendarEvent.team?.members branch in sendAddGuestsEmails (email-manager.ts:529) is unreachable and team members likely never notified

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the CalendarEvent `evt` is constructed without a `team` field (only organizer, attendees, etc.). In sendAddGuestsEmails (email-manager.ts) the team notification logic is guarded by `if (calendarEvent.team?.members) { ... }`, so with no `team` set on the input event, that branch cannot run from this handler path and team members will not be emailed. Nothing else in the diff shows `formatCalEvent` synthesizing `team`/`members` from other fields, and the booking query doesn’t include team members either.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2 — Team admin/owner check uses `&&` instead of `||` in `isTeamAdminOrOwner`, collapsing the permission to owner-only and denying team admins (who aren't owners) the ability to add guests to their team's bookings

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`, which requires the user to be both a team admin and a team owner to pass the team-based permission check. This contradicts the variable name/intent (“admin or owner”) and would deny access to team admins who are not owners, affecting the ability to add guests for team bookings.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2 — Server schema is weaker than the client contract: `guests` array has no uniqueness validation or case normalization, so duplicate or case-variant emails produce duplicate attendee rows, duplicate emails, and duplicated ICS attendees

adjudication.rationale: On the server, `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` only validates `guests` as `z.array(z.string().email())` with no uniqueness or normalization (e.g., lowercasing). In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `uniqueGuests` only filters out emails already present in `booking.attendees` and blacklisted emails, but does not dedupe duplicates within the submitted `guests` array and does not normalize case before comparisons. Those values are then inserted via `attendees.createMany` using `guestsFullDetails`, so duplicate or case-variant emails can produce multiple attendee rows and downstream duplicated attendees/ICS recipients. The client dialog *does* attempt uniqueness via a local zod refine, making the server contract weaker than the client.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2 — `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS` check is bypassable via letter case: blacklist entries are lowercased but the incoming guest email is compared raw, so case-variant blacklisted emails pass the filter and still receive emails

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, blacklist entries are normalized to lowercase (`BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS.split(...).map(email => email.toLowerCase())`), but the incoming `guest` string is compared without normalization: `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`. Since the input schema only validates email format (`z.string().email()`) and does not lowercase, a case-variant email (e.g., `Bad@Example.com`) could bypass the blacklist and be added/emailed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2 — Unbounded `guests` array (no `.max()` on the zod schema) creates an email-amplification/resource-abuse vector: any attendee can submit thousands of guests or repeatedly re-trigger emails to all participants

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `addGuests` with input schema `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` as `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` (no `.max()`), and the UI-side schema also validates an unbounded array. The handler allows any existing attendee (`isAttendee`) to call it and then sends emails via `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`, which iterates over team members and all attendees and issues `Promise.all` email sends. With no server-side cap on `guests`, a caller can submit a very large array to trigger heavy DB writes (`createMany`) and mass email sending, creating a resource-abuse / email amplification vector grounded in the shown code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2 — Calendar attendee update runs with the caller's credentials instead of the organizer's, so `updateCalendarAttendees` silently fails (or errors after persistence) for non-organizer callers, leaving calendar out of sync; credentials should come from `booking.user`

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, after allowing non-organizer callers (`isAttendee` or `isTeamAdminOrOwner`) to add guests, the code builds `EventManager` using the *caller* (`...user`) and `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`, then calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`. This means if the caller is not the booking organizer, calendar updates will run with the wrong user's credentials and can fail or no-op, leaving the organizer's destination calendar out of sync even though the booking attendees were already persisted via `prisma.booking.update(...)`. The finding’s suggested fix (use `booking.user` / organizer credentials) is directly grounded in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2 — No seats-capacity handling for seated event types: `seatsPerTimeSlot` is never enforced and no `BookingSeat` records are created, allowing overbooking beyond capacity and attendees in an inconsistent state

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuestsHandler` mutates `booking.attendees` via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` with no check against `booking.eventType?.seatsPerTimeSlot` (it only passes `seatsPerTimeSlot` through into the `CalendarEvent` object). If seated event types rely on `seatsPerTimeSlot` for capacity, this new endpoint can add arbitrary additional attendees beyond capacity, and it also does not create any seat-related records (it only creates attendee rows), which can leave seated bookings inconsistent.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3 — `findFirstOrThrow` with `booking.userId || 0` yields an unhandled Prisma error surfacing as a generic 500 instead of a clean `TRPCError` when `booking.userId` is null

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the organizer lookup does `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 }})`. If `booking.userId` is `null/undefined`, this queries `id: 0` and `findFirstOrThrow` will throw (a Prisma not-found error), which is not caught or converted into a `TRPCError` in this handler (only `sendAddGuestsEmails` is wrapped in a try/catch). This can surface as an internal error rather than a clean `TRPCError` response.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:165 — updateCalendarAttendees runs unguarded after the DB commit with no try/catch, creating an unrecoverable partial-failure state where DB, calendar, and emails become inconsistent and retries are permanently blocked by the uniqueness filter

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the DB is updated first via `prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)`, and only afterward `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);` is called with no `try/catch` or transactional rollback. If the calendar update throws, the booking already contains the new attendees, creating an inconsistent state (DB updated, external calendar not). A subsequent retry with the same guest emails will be blocked because `uniqueGuests` filters out emails already present in `booking.attendees`, leading to `uniqueGuests.length === 0` and a `BAD_REQUEST` (`emails_must_be_unique_valid`), preventing a retry of the calendar sync.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:158-163 — EventManager is built with the actor's credentials instead of the booking owner's, so when an attendee or team admin adds guests to someone else's booking the calendar event's attendee list is silently never updated

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, the mutation permits non-organizers to add guests (it allows team admin/owner and even existing attendees via `isAttendee`). However, the calendar update is performed with an EventManager instantiated from the acting user (`const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user); const eventManager = new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: [...credentials] });`), not the booking owner/organizer. The booking owner’s credentials are actually fetched via `booking.user.include.credentials` but never used. If an attendee or team admin adds guests to someone else’s booking, the actor likely lacks the organizer’s calendar credentials, so `updateCalendarAttendees` cannot reliably update the organizer’s calendar event, causing incorrect/broken behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:46-48 — authorization uses isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...) instead of ||, so team admins get FORBIDDEN even though the UI exposes the Add guests action on team bookings

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`, which requires the user to be both admin and owner. The subsequent permission gate `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee)` will therefore reject a team admin who is not also the team owner (and not organizer/attendee) with `FORBIDDEN`. This is consistent with the finding and is verifiable in the diff; the UI also adds the “additional_guests” action in `BookingListItem.tsx` without any role check, making the mismatch user-visible.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:70-78 + addGuests.schema.ts:5 — no server-side dedupe or case normalization: duplicate emails in one batch create duplicate attendee rows, and case variants bypass both the existing-attendee check and the BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS blacklist

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, `uniqueGuests` is computed via `guests.filter(...)` but there is no server-side dedupe of duplicates within the `guests` array, so the same email repeated in one request will be passed through and included multiple times in `createMany`, potentially creating duplicate attendee rows. Additionally, `blacklistedGuestEmails` are lowercased, but `guest` is not normalized (nor are `booking.attendees[].email`), so case variants (e.g., `Test@x.com`) can bypass both `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` and the existing-attendee check `guest === attendee.email`. The schema (addGuests.schema.ts) also doesn’t enforce uniqueness/case normalization server-side.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.schema.ts:5 — the guests array has no .max() cap and the handler imposes no limit, allowing a single request to create thousands of attendee rows and trigger unbounded synchronous email fan-out (resource exhaustion and mail-spam vector)

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:26-56 — no booking.status validation, so guests can be added to cancelled/rejected/pending bookings and new guests receive a CONFIRMED ICS REQUEST that resurrects a cancelled meeting in their calendars

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:167-171 — email failures are swallowed with console.log, with no detailed logging, error tracking, or retry, causing silent partial failure while the mutation returns success

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:58-68 — findFirstOrThrow on booking.userId || 0 throws a raw Prisma P2025 error instead of a TRPCError when booking.userId is null, giving the client an opaque 500 instead of a meaningful handled error

adjudication_records.issue_text: Partial-failure state with no recovery path in addGuests.handler.ts:92-102 vs :157: attendees are persisted before updateCalendarAttendees runs unguarded; if it throws, guests are in the DB but the mutation errors, and retry dead-ends because the dedupe filter matches all guests and throws BAD_REQUEST, with no way to remove attendees

adjudication_records.issue_text: Misleading reused error key in addGuests.handler.ts:80-81: when all provided guests are duplicates/already attending, the handler throws emails_must_be_unique_valid ('Emails must be unique and valid'), which doesn't describe the actual problem and is surfaced verbatim to the user

adjudication_records.issue_text: booking.userId || 0 into findFirstOrThrow in addGuests.handler.ts:58-60: booking.userId is nullable; a null value becomes id: 0 and surfaces as an unhandled Prisma P2025 (500) rather than a proper TRPCError

adjudication_records.issue_text: No booking-status validation in addGuests.handler.ts — guests can be added to cancelled/pending/rejected bookings, triggering 'confirmed' ICS REQUEST attachments and 'your event is scheduled' emails for dead meetings (correctness bug and mild phishing/spam vector)

adjudication_records.issue_text: EventManager built from the acting user's credentials instead of the organizer's in addGuests.handler.ts:149-154 — fetched booking.user.credentials are never used; for non-organizer actors, updateCalendarAttendees runs against the wrong calendar account so the organizer's calendar event never gets the new attendees

adjudication_records.issue_text: Non-atomic partial failure: DB write commits before calendar/email steps in addGuests.handler.ts — if updateCalendarAttendees throws, the mutation 500s after attendees are already in the DB, and retries are rejected by the dedup filter with misleading emails_must_be_unique_valid error

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email failures swallowed in addGuests.handler.ts:158-162 — catch block only console.logs and success is returned unconditionally, so the client shows 'Guests added' success toast even if every email send failed; also uses console.log instead of structured logging

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email normalization missing in addGuests.handler.ts:66-74 — blacklist entries are lowercased but guest emails are not, so 'Spam@x.com' bypasses blacklist entry 'spam@x.com'; same case-sensitivity in the attendee-dedup check creates duplicate attendee rows

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unbounded guests array (no max() on z.array in addGuests.schema.ts) with no rate limiting, combined with attendee authorization path — any authenticated attendee on any booking can create thousands of attendee rows and trigger thousands of invite emails in a single API call (email-bombing vector)

adjudication_records.issue_text: No server-side uniqueness within a request — uniqueness refine exists only in the client dialog; direct API calls with duplicate emails pass the schema and createMany inserts duplicate attendee rows, with no unique constraint to prevent concurrent request races

adjudication.rationale: The server-side input schema `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts) only validates `guests` as `z.array(z.string().email())` and does not enforce uniqueness. adjudication_records.issue_text: isInvalidEmail never reset on success in AddGuestsDialog.tsx:33-38 — onSuccess resets emails and closes the dialog but not isInvalidEmail, so reopening shows the stale 'Emails must be unique and valid' banner before any input
